blocks.text: This Name is found in the previous hadeeth of Ya'alaa bin Umayyah who narrated that,

"The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man washing in a public place without a lower garment. So he mounted the pulpit, praised and extolled Allah and said: Allah is The One possessing honourable shame (Hayyiy) and The Concealer (Sitteer), He loves modesty and concealment. So when any of you washes, he should conceal himself."
Ibn Abee Haatim narrated in his tafseer and Al-Bayhaqi in 'As-Sunan al-Kubraa' from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbaas who said,

"Two men asked him about seeking permission in the three times of privacy which Allaah ordered in the Qur'aan. So Ibn 'Abbaas said, "Indeed Allaah is the Concealer of sins, He loves concealment. People did not have curtains on their doors nor alcoves in their houses. It was possible that a man would be caught by his servant, son or orphan in his room while he was with his wife. So Allaah ordered them to seek permission (to enter) in those times of privacy that Allaah named. Then afterwards curtains came. Allaah increased them in wealth so they put up curtains and had alcoves. People then saw that as enough instead of seeking the permission that was ordered."
blocks.ref: Ibn Abee Haatim, Tafseer; Al-Bayhaqi, As-Sunan al-Kubraa (the times of privacy referred to are in Noor 24:58)

blocks.text: Its chain was authenticated by Ibn Katheer in his Tafseer.

As-Sitteer means the One who conceals His servants frequently. He does not embarrass them openly. He wants His servants to conceal themselves from that which would embarrass them, disgrace them and dishonour. This is a bounty, mercy, forbearance and generosity from Allaah. A servant may fall into something of sins and disobedience, even though he is in dire need of his Lord. With this the Lord despite being perfectly free of need from any of His creation and from their obedience and worship, He honours His servant, conceals his faults and is shy from uncovering him, dishonouring him and making the punishment of him permissible.
He leads him to the means of concealment and grants him success to regret and repent. He pardons and forgives him. This is from His mercy and subtleness towards His creation. Allaah said,
And He it is Who accepts repentance from His slaves, and forgives sins, and He knows what you do.

For this reason Allaah dislikes from His servants that they spread it and advertise when they fall into disobedience. He calls them to repent from it to Allaah between them and Him. Allaah conceals and covers him, not to let any person know. The most hated person is the one who spends the night as a sinner with Allaah concealing him then in the morning he removes the concealment that Allaah afforded him.
In the two Saheehs from Abee Hurayrah who said,

I heard Allah's Messenger ﷺ saying, "All the sins of my followers will be forgiven except those who commit a sin openly or disclose their sins to the people. An example of such disclosure is that a person commits a sin at night and though Allah screens it from the public, then he comes in the morning, and says, 'O so-and-so, I did such-and-such (evil) deed yesterday,' though he spent his night screened by his Lord (none knowing about his sin) and in the morning he removes Allah's screen from himself."

This is where the meaning comes from where 'sitr' concealment of Allaah's servants is not removing their screen or looking for their private faults. In the two Saheehs, Ibn 'Umar said that the Prophet ﷺ said,
"Whoever conceals the faults of a Muslim, Allaah will conceal his faults on the Day of Resurrection."
O Allaah! Cover our defects and faults, forgive us our sins and slips and let our deeds and lives be sealed with good deeds.

keyPoints: As-Sitteer is found in the hadeeth of Ya'alaa bin Umayyah: "Allah is ... The Concealer (Sitteer), He loves modesty and concealment."
As-Sitteer means the One who conceals His servants frequently and does not embarrass them openly.
Despite being free of need of His creation, Allaah conceals His sinning servant's faults, is shy from exposing him, and leads him to regret, repent and be forgiven.
Allaah dislikes that His servants advertise their sins; the most hated person is the one Allaah concealed at night who then exposes himself in the morning.

From the meaning of 'sitr' is concealing the faults of Allaah's servants and not looking for their private faults: "Whoever conceals the faults of a Muslim, Allaah will conceal his faults on the Day of Resurrection."

evidence.text: "Allah is The One possessing honourable shame (Hayyiy) and The Concealer (Sitteer), He loves modesty and concealment."
"All the sins of my followers will be forgiven except those who commit a sin openly or disclose their sins to the people..."

recall.a: The Concealer of sins: the One who conceals His servants frequently and does not embarrass them openly.

recall.q: Which Companion described Allaah as 'the Concealer of sins, He loves concealment' when asked about the three times of privacy?
recall.a: Ibn 'Abbaas (narrated by Ibn Abee Haatim and Al-Bayhaqi; its chain authenticated by Ibn Katheer).

recall.q: Who is the most hated person regarding concealment, according to the chapter?
recall.a: The one who spends the night as a sinner with Allaah concealing him, then in the morning removes the concealment that Allaah afforded him.

recall.q: What reward is promised for concealing the faults of a Muslim?
recall.a: "Allaah will conceal his faults on the Day of Resurrection" (Bukhaaree and Muslim, from Ibn 'Umar).
